name: Greenhaven World Server
author: otterdays
description: Greenhaven MMORPG world server (rpg-server, Rust/Axum WebSocket): one prebuilt, fully static Linux x86_64 binary. Nothing is compiled on this node and no credentials are needed - the installer downloads the release asset and verifies its SHA-256 before installing it. ONE TCP port only (WebSocket /ws and HTTP /health share it); no UDP, no query port. No config files: every setting is an environment variable, so change them as egg variables, not as files. The only value an operator must fill is RELEASE_BASE, the release download prefix. The save is data/world.sqlite plus its -wal and -shm sidecars under /home/container/data and survives reinstall. Boot detection matches the line 'world listening on ws://'. The map JSON is required at boot and is shipped in the release; the database is created on first boot if absent. Guide: server-architecture/PELICAN-EGG.md.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Greenhaven world install: prebuilt static binary, no toolchain on this node.
# Safe to re-run: it replaces the binary and the map and never touches data/.
set -e
cd /mnt/server
# The release stamp is the one thing a restart cannot show you: it is rewritten on every
# install and printed at boot as the installed release.
rm -f greenhaven-release.txt
if [ -z "${RELEASE_BASE}" ]; then
  echo "RELEASE_BASE is not set. Set it to the release download prefix, for example https://github.com/<owner>/<releases-repo>/releases/download/v0.1.0"
  exit 1
fi
BIN_ASSET="greenhaven-server-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl"
MAP_ASSET="greenhaven.json"
fetch() {
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then curl -fsSL "$1" -o "$2";
  elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then wget -qO "$2" "$1";
  else echo "neither curl nor wget is present in this install image"; exit 1; fi
}
mkdir -p data assets/maps
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
echo "Fetching ${RELEASE_BASE}/${BIN_ASSET} ..."
fetch "${RELEASE_BASE}/${BIN_ASSET}" "${tmp}/${BIN_ASSET}"
echo "Verifying the SHA-256 ..."
fetch "${RELEASE_BASE}/${BIN_ASSET}.sha256" "${tmp}/sum"
expected="$(awk '{print $1}' "${tmp}/sum")"
actual="$(sha256sum "${tmp}/${BIN_ASSET}" | awk '{print $1}')"
if [ -z "${expected}" ]; then echo "the checksum file is empty - a release must publish ${BIN_ASSET}.sha256"; exit 1; fi
if [ "${expected}" != "${actual}" ]; then echo "checksum mismatch: expected ${expected}, got ${actual}"; exit 1; fi
mv "${tmp}/${BIN_ASSET}" greenhaven-server
chmod +x greenhaven-server
echo "Fetching ${RELEASE_BASE}/${MAP_ASSET} ..."
fetch "${RELEASE_BASE}/${MAP_ASSET}" assets/maps/greenhaven.json
test -s assets/maps/greenhaven.json || { echo "the map download is empty"; exit 1; }
rm -rf "${tmp}"
test -x greenhaven-server || { echo "no executable was installed"; exit 1; }
echo "${RELEASE_BASE}" > greenhaven-release.txt
# The binary takes no CLI flags: never execute it here, it would bind a port.
echo "Install complete. The map is validated on boot; a damaged map stops the boot rather than the world."
exit 0

variables.name: Release download base
variables.description: Release download prefix (base URL). Currently the published v0.1.6 release. The installer fetches <RELEASE_BASE>/greenhaven-server-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, its .sha256, and <RELEASE_BASE>/greenhaven.json. To update the world, bump this string to the newer release and reinstall. On success the installer also writes greenhaven-release.txt next to the binary, which the server prints at boot as `Installed release` beside the `Requested release` it reads from this variable; a mismatch means the server was not reinstalled. Admin-only.

variables.name: Debug world endpoint
variables.description: 1 exposes /debug/world (live atlas dump). Leave 0 on a public host: it is off by default on a non-loopback bind. Admin-only: changing this needs a server restart.
